sections.skill: Strategy: reflect one cell at a time
sections.relationship: Students who pick a rotated or unflipped shape usually try to picture the whole shape at once. Reflecting one cell at a time (same row, same distance on the other side) makes every reflection checkable.
sections.author_note: Students who pick a rotated or unflipped shape usually try to picture the whole shape at once. Reflecting one cell at a time (same row, same distance on the other side) makes every reflection checkable.

lesson.title: Reflect one cell at a time
text: A mirror line acts like a fold. Each point keeps its distance from the line but ends up on the other side. Points on the line stay where they are.
For a vertical mirror line, a cell keeps its row and only its column changes. For a horizontal mirror line, a cell keeps its column and only its row changes.
So reflect one cell at a time: count how far it is from the line, then count the same distance on the other side. Check two or three cells; if any one is wrong, the figure is not the reflection.

example.title: Worked example (a different figure)
prompt: A grid has 6 rows. A horizontal mirror line lies between rows 3 and 4. A shape has cells at row 1 column 2, row 2 column 2 and row 3 column 5. Where is its reflection?
steps: Row 3 is 1 row above the line, so its image is 1 row below it: row 4. Row 2 goes to row 5 and row 1 to row 6.
Columns do not change in a horizontal mirror.
Image: row 6 column 2, row 5 column 2 and row 4 column 5.
Quick check: each cell and its image add up to 7 rows (1 + 6, 2 + 5, 3 + 4), the same for every pair, because the line is halfway between them.

questions.prompt: A row of 12 cells is numbered 1 to 12. A mirror line lies between cells 6 and 7. Give two cell numbers a and b, with a less than b, that are mirror images of each other.
questions.rule: a + b == 13 and a < b and a >= 1 and b <= 12 and isInteger(a) and isInteger(b)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: a + b == 13 and a < b and a >= 1 and b <= 12 and isInteger(a) and isInteger(b) (example: a = 4, b = 9)
